system.summary: Two-part numeric code of about 2,450 groups for syllables, words and names, homophonic, with local alphabetical runs and 5-figure nulls.
system.notes: Runs such as 2201 che, 2205 ci, 2211 di, 2221 fi, 2230 l, 2231 l', 2232 la and 2082-2084 del, dell', della are alphabetical; the runs themselves are scattered. R9586/R9588 use a second code and have their own entry (r9586).

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear decipherments on R9566 p3 (first ten lines), R9569, R9571 and R9589, in ASNa busta 2337; no printed decipherment found.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE session cookie, Claude Code with Opus 5, problem posed with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched metadata for DECODE R9542-R9590 through the API and the 28 images of the target and of box 2317/2337 siblings with the shared cookie.
Web search for a printed or published decipherment of the 1816-19 Castelcicala despatches.
Transcribed 331 groups from R9553 p.1, R9582 and R9585; identified the recipient (Circello) and the code name (Cifra della Segreteria di Stato).
Compared with the box 2317 record R9549 that DECODE suggests holds the plaintexts: its cipher uses a different code (frequent groups 441, 486, 563, 1144; range to ~1999).
Checked the decrypted box 2337 siblings: 1850s-60s telegrams and letters in other codes.
Frequency and repeat count: 208 distinct groups in 331 over a ~2,500-group code, repeated multi-group phrases; too little text for a ciphertext-only attack.
DECODE API metadata for R9532-R9591 and 100 page images fetched with the session cookie.
Web search for a printed decipherment of Castelcicala's Paris despatches.
Neighbouring 'Decrypted' records of busta 2337 checked for the same code: R9569, R9571 and R9589 (1823) share it and carry interlinear glosses; R9590 (1830) is another code.
All 27 records transcribed from full-resolution crops by two sub-agents (9,400 main-code groups); R9566 p3 found to carry a contemporary interlinear decipherment.
Glosses aligned group by group: about 110 values, syllabic and word-level, homophonic; 5-figure groups fall where the gloss has nothing (nulls); local alphabetical runs noticed.
Key extended by hand from repeated contexts (1714 = i, 2318 = ta and ~50 weaker values); 46% of groups get a value.
Per-group candidate scoring with the it-modern 5-gram LM over known neighbours (length bonus, then PMI): no discrimination between candidates.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 4482 tokens, 260 types, it-modern order 4: reading -1.831 per letter; random keys -2.472 (z 7.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.84 (mean -1.86, z 2.1); annealer on the real text -1.811. Verdict: underdetermined.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from castelcicala1816, which had included R9586 and R9588, two Castelcicala letters in a different code (values about 100-1100), with the despatches in the Segreteria di Stato code. This profile keeps the Segreteria di Stato code (25 documents) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per-record transcriptions transcripts/R*.txt (with the contemporary glosses) and cipher/R*.txt; decryption reading_partial.txt (apply.py partial decode, converted from Latin-1 to UTF-8, text unchanged), and the interlinear glosses for R9566, R9569, R9571, R9589; key.tsv. Most letters have only a partial decode: no full decryption exists.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). reading_partial.txt read letter by letter: about half the groups have no value, with unread groups between nearly every pair of known words (docs/_check_reading.py: 2 of 24 sentences clean); no sentence of the 23 despatches without a full gloss can be built. They are relabelled decoded, not read (R9566 and R9569 have only fragmentary glosses). R9571 and R9589 read as Italian from their contemporary interlinear decipherments (reading_review A). Method key recovered based on adjacent plaintext -> read from existing decipherment (parts); fraction_read 0.467 -> 0.026.

Re-read of the 23 decoded-not-read despatches under REREAD_BRIEF (batch mix1): every transcript checked for a gloss (none beyond R9566 p. 3, R9569, R9571, R9589), no edition, code book not online; coverage and longest known run measured per document (0.19-0.68; runs of 3-14 groups outside the glosses); hand retry on R9566 p. 3 ll. 10-14 against the Floridas crib fixed no new value (17 of 37 groups open). All 23 stay decoded, not read; blocker no-key-material (reread_log.md).

v3 verification: R9571 scored on transcripts/R9571.txt (gloss interleaved with code groups, 0.577). The gloss lines joined into transcripts/R9571_reading.md: 1.0 explicit-hole and plain. Keeps read; the stale decoded-not-read note on the entry removed.

Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): R9589 was scored on its gloss-and-groups transcription file (plain 0.385). The contemporary interlinear decipherment written out as transcripts/R9589_reading.md with English R9589_en.md: plain 0.8, explicit 0.8. Keeps read.

Consistency pass (cl): the Remaining gaps line 'R9571, R9589: English translation not yet written' (not-attempted) was stale: transcripts/R9571_en.md and R9589_en.md exist and are the texts' translation fields; moved to Closed. documents[].read for R9569 read -> read in part, matching its texts state (decoded, not read).

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent check of key.tsv against the contemporary interlinear glosses (verify_dudout_20261114.py reads only key.tsv and transcripts/R*.txt). On each glossed line, the key values that occur in order in the gloss letters: G 180/215, X 30/41, I 54/70; the misses are the decipherer's abbreviations (Minro, Cte, Fra, Sigr), groups left unglossed, and the faint pencil glosses on R9563 pp. 2-3 (which the re-read log missed). Readings corrected from the groups under the gloss (G/X values only): R9571 'Vo...' has no group (car-di-na-le cas-ti-gli-one), 'Pontefica[te]' is pon-ti-fi-ca-to, 'Francia. L'Austria per la' is 'Francia e l'Austria per l''; in R9589 the '[…]' counted group 1450 twice (it is the group under 'avuto'). v10_relabel share R9571 0.961 -> 1.0, R9589 0.974 -> 0.987; class unchanged. Not checked on the images (DECODE, not held). VERIFY_dudout_20261114.md.

Project check of PR #572 (Brice Dudout): his key-against-gloss script re-run (G 180/215, X 30/41, I 54/70). The four corrected places looked up again in key.tsv: R9571 2009 2211 1725 2295 2012 2448 1535 2169 = car-di-na-le cas-ti-gli-one (no group under 'Vo...'), 1609 2448 2221 1951 2450 = pon-ti-fi-ca-to, 2353 332 2231 383 = Francia e l'Austria; R9589 1450 2232 2357 1758 2318 = ? la li-ber-ta. v10_relabel.measure: R9571 1.0, R9589 0.987, both stay read. The page quotation of R9571 corrected. Recorded in NOTES, not changed in key.tsv: 1050 = ciò (I) clashes with 2268 = ciò in R9571 l. 11; 1161 = su-o/a; R9563 pp. 2-3 and R9561 carry a few faint pencil gloss words, so the per-record notes of those two entries are corrected. DECODE images not held.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.831; polyphony 0.0; 4946 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -1.811

outcome.method_basis: R9571 and R9589 (1823) are read from their contemporary interlinear decipherments; the other 23 despatches decode with the key rebuilt from those glosses (162 values) only into fragments, with unread groups between nearly every pair of words.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: only documents that build sentences count. R9571 (131 groups) and R9589 (113) read from their contemporary glosses: 244 of 9,428 groups (documents[].length) = 0.026. Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.467 (cipher/<R>.txt against key.tsv, 4,340 of 9,286 groups with a key value, recounted 14 Oct 2026), which measures key coverage, not sentences.
outcome.notes: fraction_read = share of main-code groups in the target letters of catalogue 166 and 167 with any key value (key.tsv grades G/X/I; about a third of the values are unconfirmed inferences). No letter reads through; sender/recipient, dates and code structure established. Remeasured 21 Sept 2026 over all 27 documents: 0.429 (was 0.447). Having a value is not reading: no letter reads through. R9569/R9571/R9589 marked read on their contemporary interlinear decipherments. Split 14 Oct 2026: R9586/R9588 (another code) moved to r9586; fraction recounted on the 25 main-code documents: 0.467.

texts.label: R9566, 1 Dec 1816 (no. 3874; plus a fragment in another hand)
texts.summary: Despatch 3874 to the Marchese di Circello: its contemporary interlinear decipherment (first ten lines of p. 3) reports that the Interior Minister Decazes, high in the King of France's favour, met the Spanish minister Onís on his way through and spoke of the cession of the Floridas and of the rumoured cession of Cuba to England. A fragment in another hand is bound with it.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (reread_log.md): the contemporary gloss covers only p. 3 ll. 1-9, one sentence (Decazes, Onís, the Floridas and Cuba); the other five pages (with the fragment in another hand) have no gloss and key.tsv gives a value to 0.56 of the groups. A hand retry on the unglossed continuation (p. 3 ll. 10-14: "desidera della Francia [..] e la [..] ... la Spagna ...") left 17 of 37 groups open and fixed no new value. Blocker: no-key-material.

texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (reread_log.md): the gloss of p. 1 ll. 8-16 gives one sentence through the decipherer’s syllable splits ("... ed io ho motivo di credere di no, e che [...] la suddetta elezione la Francia gli darebbe l’esclusiva"); p. 1 ll. 1-7 and p. 2 (out of focus) have no gloss and decode at the usual half coverage (0.68 overall). One sentence of about ten. Blocker: no-key-material.

texts.label: R9571, 8 Sep 1823
texts.summary: Castelcicala to Cavaliere Luigi de' Medici: France wants Cardinal Castiglioni as Pope, the Duc de Laval is blamed, and France and Austria have no accord on the election. Read from its contemporary interlinear decipherment.

reading_review.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: the sweep scored transcripts/R9571.txt with the code-group lines interleaved with the gloss (0.577), a false alarm. The contemporary interlinear decipherment (the P: lines) joined into running text in transcripts/R9571_reading.md: 1.0 explicit-hole and plain (5/5 sentences, 50 words; 'Vo...' abbreviation and the struck 'te' counted as holes).

texts.label: R9589, 9 Oct 1823
texts.summary: Castelcicala to Cavaliere Luigi de' Medici: the Spanish king's liberty, and the Duc d'Angoulême not expected back for two months. Read from its contemporary interlinear decipherment.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1823, Italian: plain share is a bar too): the sweep scored transcripts/R9589.txt, the interlinear gloss interleaved with code-group lines and notes (plain 0.385, explicit 0.654). The contemporary interlinear decipherment written out as running text, transcripts/R9589_reading.md (gloss lines joined, clear lines in ⟨ ⟩, the unglossed first group […] and the doubtful first gloss word [?avuto] marked): plain 0.8 (8/10), explicit 0.8 (8/10). The sentences hold. Keeps read. The entry's old note (partial key decode, no sentence) concerned the key decode, not this decipherment, and is dropped. Earlier: The contemporary interlinear decipherment in transcripts/R9589.txt reads as continuous Italian (the King of Spain's liberty, the despatch in cipher no. 688, the Duc d'Angouleme not back for two months). Low score from the interleaved code-group lines.

texts.label: R9553, 1 Apr 1816
texts.summary: Despatch of Fabrizio Ruffo, principe di Castelcicala, Neapolitan ambassador, to the Marchese di Circello in Naples (1 Apr 1816), in the Segreteria di Stato code. Only the groups with a value in key.tsv decode (section ## R9553 of reading_partial.txt); no passage reads through.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (reread_log.md): no contemporary gloss on this record (only R9566 p. 3, R9569, R9571, R9589 have one), no edition, no code book online. key.tsv gives a value to 0.40 of its groups and the longest run of known groups is 5, so an unknown group falls inside nearly every clause; a hand retry on the best unglossed stretch (R9566 p. 3 ll. 10-14) fixed no new value. Blocker: no-key-material (the 1816-19 Cifra della Segreteria di Stato, ASNa Esteri).
